evidence.title: Undeclared consumers and hidden feedback can couple otherwise separate systems
evidence.observation: Source-reported finding: The authors describe how outputs used without declared dependencies can couple systems, and how apparently separate systems can influence one another through users or markets. A local improvement may worsen system behavior. Observation period and measurement context: Engineering analysis and illustrative patterns; no population observation period.
evidence.evidence_standing: Source-reported bounded account; Conceptual engineering analysis; not independently reproduced
evidence.glossary_fit: Illustrative or qualifying; does not validate a definition

source_locations.SRC-138: Introduction, §2 Undeclared Consumers, §4 Hidden Feedback Loops, monitoring discussion

evidence.limitations: Engineering analysis rather than a controlled trial, effect-size estimate or LLM-agent prevalence measurement. Mitigations and strategic reasons for technical debt are discussed. The 2014 precursor full text was inaccessible.
evidence.open_questions: Transfer to other populations, tasks and operating environments remains unestablished. Missing measurement details are not inferred.
evidence.support_assessment: Commons interpretation: An unrecognized consequential connection can remain outside an observer’s frame even when component activities are visible.

terms.name: Beyond visual range (BVR)
terms.definition: A condition in which consequential actions, effects, or causal relationships fall outside what an observer recognizes as relevant to the process being examined. Those activities may be visible elsewhere, yet the connection that makes them consequential is unrecognized. Neither concealment nor a defective local monitor is required.

terms.name: Cross-system feedback
terms.definition: A pattern in which an action or output from one technical or organizational process affects activity elsewhere and subsequent responses modify conditions for additional participants. Many response paths may exist; there need not be a single linear loop.

relationships.explanation: Conceptual illustration of an unrecognized consequential dependency; not empirical validation of the proposed BVR category.
Describes coupling through undeclared consumers and hidden feedback.
